I haven't changed anything. This app has a firm rule that database changes can only add things, never delete them, so I can't remove the feedback table myself.

**What the rule protects:** once the app is live, the saved feedback is real data. Deleting the table erases every entry for good, and there's no undo. It could also break the live app while the update rolls out. For that reason only an engineer can remove a table, deliberately and outside the normal workflow.

**What the feedback table is:** it holds everything people send with the **"Report a problem"** button, and the staff list of those reports reads from it. Engineers also use it to turn problem reports into new changes, so it's more connected than it may look.

**Your options:**

1. **Hide the feature, keep the data (recommended).** Remove the "Report a problem" button and the reports list, so nobody can see or add feedback. The existing entries stay stored, untouched, and can be brought back if needed. I can do this through the normal process, starting with `/yolo-sdlc:idea`. It takes a minute and records why the change was made.
2. **Ask an engineer to delete the table permanently.** If the stored feedback really has to go (for example, for a privacy reason), an engineer needs to do it. Say why in your request so they can decide how to handle the existing entries.
3. **Leave it as it is.** The table does nothing unless someone uses the button.

I couldn't ask you which you prefer in this session. If you want option 1, reply "go ahead with option 1" and I'll start the idea record.

I've written up the sick leave examples, but they aren't agreed yet. I couldn't put the approval questions to you in this session, so the idea stays a draft until you confirm.

**The draft examples**
1. When I (Jane Doe) open "Sick leave", enter 5–6 Oct 2026, type "Flu" as the diagnosis and press Save, I see "Sick leave recorded" and the entry appears under "My sick leave".
2. When someone on the HR team opens "Sick leave", they see everyone's sick days in one list, newest first, including Jane Doe, 5–6 Oct 2026, "Flu".
3. When I press Save with no dates, or with an end date before the start date, I see "Please enter the dates you were off sick" and nothing is added.
4. When John Smith, who isn't on the HR team, opens "Sick leave", they see only their own entries and never Jane's dates or diagnosis.

**What will change for people**
- A new "Sick leave" page appears in the side menu.
- Staff record a start date, an end date and the diagnosis. Their name comes from their sign-in.
- Each person sees only their own entries. Only the HR team sees everyone's.
- An engineer sets up the list of people who count as the HR team, because the app can't yet tell HR apart from other staff.

**Review needed:** This one gets an engineer review before it goes live, because it stores staff health information.

**Company rules this touches (none are signed off yet):**
- **Health data:** a diagnosis counts as sensitive, so the person responsible for this data (I assumed the HR lead) must agree in writing before anything is built.
- **Collect only what's needed:** does HR really need the diagnosis, or just "off sick with a doctor's note: yes/no"? Dropping the diagnosis removes the health-data sign-off and makes this quicker to ship.
- **How long it's kept:** we need to agree how long sick-leave entries are stored before they're deleted.
- **Official record:** if this replaces the emailed doctor's notes as the official sick-leave record, the HR lead needs to agree to that.

I've recorded all of this in the idea's notes and marked each rule "waiting for HR" or "waiting for HR lead".

**To move forward, run `/yolo-sdlc:shape` again and tell me:**
1. Are these examples right, do any need changing, or is something missing?
2. Should we keep the diagnosis, or store only "doctor's note received"?
3. Has the HR lead already agreed, or will you ask them first?

report.reply:
I went through everything recorded for this app: 4 problems, all from the leave tracker and leave calendar changes. Nothing is written yet. This step needs your approval, and I can't ask for it in this session.

## What keeps coming back

**Dates showing a day early (3 of 4 problems)**
- The builder's checker flagged it twice, in two different changes: leave tracker round 2 (`leave.vue`, UTC dates) and leave calendar round 2 (`calendar.vue`, `toISOString()`).
- The pull request review flagged it again on PR #8 (`leave.vue`, `toLocaleDateString` with no time zone). The suggested fix was `formatDate()`.

`CLAUDE.md` already says "Show dates with `formatDate()`", but builds missed it three times. So these lessons make that rule more specific instead of repeating it.

**Left out:** the "Sumbit" typo on the Save button. It happened once, so it's not a repeat.

## Proposed lessons

1. **For building:** `Leave pages (app/pages/leave.vue, calendar.vue): show every date with formatDate() from app/utils/locale.ts, never toISOString() or toLocaleDateString(); both shift leave days a day early in Vietnam time.`
   *Evidence:* verifier ×2 (leave tracker round 2, leave calendar round 2), review ×1 (PR #8)

2. **For review:** `Warn on any toISOString(), toLocaleDateString() or toLocaleString() used to display a date in app/pages/; it must go through formatDate() (PR #8, two verifier rounds).`
   *Evidence:* same 3 findings

**Lessons to remove:** none. `LEARNED.md` is empty.

## Possible plugin issue (draft, not filed)

This problem may not be specific to this app, because the builder ignored an existing `CLAUDE.md` rule. Here's a draft issue for `tammai/yolo-sdlc`:

> **Title:** Catch hand-rolled date formatting in `pnpm check`
> **Body:** In one app, the implementer used `toISOString()` / `toLocaleDateString()` for displayed dates three times across two intents, even though CLAUDE.md says to use `formatDate()`. Each time the verifier or reviewer caught it, which cost a rework round. Suggestion: add a check (lint rule or grep in the check script) that flags these calls in `app/pages/` and `app/components/`, and have the implementer agent search for them before handing off.

## Next step

Choose which to add: **1**, **2**, **both**, or **neither**, and whether to file the plugin issue. My recommendation is both lessons. They're short, and together they cover the building step and the review step.

Once you confirm, I'll:
- add the chosen lessons to `LEARNED.md` on a new `learn/2026-09-29` branch
- commit it as "Learn: 2 lessons"
- ship it with `/yolo-sdlc:ship`. It will be red tier because `LEARNED.md` is engineer-owned, so it gets the engineer review.

One thing to know: `leave.vue` and `calendar.vue` aren't in this checkout. I'm going only by the recorded problems and couldn't see how those pages show dates now.

Here's how delivery is going, based on the last merged changes:

| Stage | Metric | Value | Based on |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 Plan | idea → examples agreed (median) | 20 min | 3 PRs |
| 2 Design | changes whose examples were reworked after the build started | 33% | 3 PRs |
| 3 Build | verification passed first time (no verifier round) | 67% | 3 PRs |
| 3 Build | plan → built (median) | 50 min | 3 PRs |
| 4 Test | first ci run passed | 67% | 3 PRs |
| 5 Deploy | pull request open → merged (median) | 30 min | 3 PRs |
| 5 Deploy | reviews with warnings | 50% | 2 PRs |
| 5 Deploy | warnings shipped as they were (last review, total) | 2 | 2 PRs |
| 5 Deploy | merges to main per week (deploys) | 3.0 | 3 PRs |
| 6 Maintain | changes that came from a problem report | 0% | 3 PRs |

**What this means:**
- **Speed looks good.** Agreeing examples takes about 20 minutes, building about 50, and merging about 30. The team shipped about 3 changes a week.
- **None of the changes started from a user's problem report.** So what people run into in the live app isn't feeding back into the work yet.
- **Two review warnings went live without being fixed.** An engineer should check whether either one matters.
- **Each of the other checks tripped once:** one change had its examples rewritten after building began, one needed a second build round, and one failed its first automated check. With only three changes, that's normal noise, not a pattern.

**One thing to try:** have an engineer run `/yolo-sdlc:triage`. It turns problem reports from the live app into draft ideas, so what users hit becomes the next change.

**What the numbers can't show:** this covers only 3 changes, and just 2 for the review numbers, so a single change moves any percentage by about a third. Treat these as early signals, not trends. Work done before this workflow was set up has no stage times, so it isn't counted.
